attempted_claim: Let C be a connected skeletal finite EI-category with exactly two isomorphism types of objects {x,y}, finite automorphism groups G=Aut_C(x) and H=Aut_C(y), exactly one nonzero directed hom-biset (say C(x,y)=M nonempty finite (H,G)-biset and C(y,x) empty), and let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 dividing |G||H| with M transitive as (H,G)-biset. Determine for every such pair (C,k) whether the category algebra kC has finite or infinite representation type, and when finite the exact number of isomorphism classes of finite-dimensional indecomposable kC-modules. A complete answer proves a necessary and sufficient finite-versus-infinite criterion expressed only in terms of G,H,p, the point stabilizers of M, and the modular representation data of kG and kH, with the exact indecomposable count in each finite-type case, or else rigorously disproves uniformity by exhibiting an explicit infinite family where the stated parameters do not decide the dichotomy.
claim_type: finite versus infinite dichotomy with exact count or nonuniformity disproof
decisive_failure: The standard idempotent-corner argument establishes only a necessary cyclic-Sylow condition for finite representation type and cannot yield the required sufficiency or exact indecomposable counts. The bounded Goursat and permutation-top computations confirm genuine coarse-parameter collisions but prove no representation-type separation, and the minimal undecided algebras all sit at bimodule-top dimension one with loops on both Ext-quiver vertices where no locally available criterion applies.
